subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice — great meeting earlier, thanks for carving out the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the TTFT/streaming side so we can scope a perf run: 

Recap of ACME requirements (from call):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: median <= 150 ms, p95 <= 300 ms (measured from request receipt to first token byte on the wire).
- Concurrency: support ~500 concurrent active requests (burst tolerance to 800 for 30s).
- Throughput: baseline ~50 requests/sec with typical payloads; some hourly spikes up to ~120 rps.
- Streaming: client wants progressive streaming (SSE or WebSocket) for partial renders. Chunk cadence preference: small chunks every ~200–300 ms to enable UI progressive rendering; also acceptable: 2–3 chunks/sec for longer tokens.
- Security: WebSocket + token refresh support, mutual TLS not required but recommended for Dedicated/Private.

Clarifications and things we need from your side to scope perf run: 
1) Typical input size: avg prompt length (tokens/characters), median/95th.
2) Expected average and max generated tokens per response.
3) Client behavior on partial results (do you render on every chunk or debounce?).
4) Whether you require ordering guarantees across chunked messages and how you handle reconnections.

Proposed Redwood perf test plan (attached as ttft_perf-plan.xlsx):
- Test model: gptx-50b-quant (we’ll mirror if you have a preferred model).
- Measurement: TTFT measured at client-side synthetic harness (TLS handshake + request -> first byte). We’ll provide both request-received server metrics and end-to-end client measurements.
- Scenarios: steady-state 50 rps, concurrency ramps to 500/800, and spike tests. Streaming simulation to send partial chunks at 200ms cadence and variable chunk sizes.
- Acceptance: median TTFT <=150ms; p95 <=300ms for steady-state. If we see higher TTFT we’ll iterate on batching, KV cache priming, and model parallel config.

Next steps / action items:
- Alice: confirm payload averages (tokens/request) and whether your clients debounce chunk renders. Please share sample payloads (size + distribution).
- ACME: confirm a 2–4 hour perf window during next week to run tests against a staging endpoint.
- Redwood (Lauren/Lukas): scope infra and cost estimates for the test; validate model variant and caching strategy.

I’ve attached the perf plan and will follow up internally to schedule the test. Happy to jump on a short 30m sync if helpful.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A few quick clarifications: 

- Yes, TTFT must be measured end-to-end (client request to first token). We will validate on our side but prefer Redwood produce server-side timing as well for root-cause.
- We need guaranteed support for secure WebSocket (w/ token refresh) in addition to SSE; can you confirm both are supported in your staging endpoint?
- Chunk cadence: our front-end renders on every chunk, but we debounce UI updates at ~150 ms to prevent jank — so chunks every ~200 ms is ideal.

I attached a ZIP with representative sample payloads and token distributions (acme_sample_payloads.zip). Typical payload: 120–220 tokens prompt, generated tokens 40–300 depending on use case.

We’re available for a perf window next week — Wed 14 May 09:00–13:00 PT looks best for our infra team. Please confirm and we’ll open the firewall/ingress rules for the IPs you provide.

Also: can you include an experiment that measures TTFT under a cold KV cache vs. warmed KV cache? We have some highly repeatable prefixes.

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corp
alice@acme.com
